licensure.disciplinary_grounds.rationale: These nine buckets cleanly partition the data by capturing the dominant recurring themes: fraud in obtaining licenses or fees, criminal convictions, clinical incompetence/negligence/malpractice, substance abuse impairing practice, non-substance physical or mental incapacity, deceptive advertising, aiding/employing unlicensed persons or misusing one's own license, general unprofessional conduct (including sexual misconduct, fee-splitting, solicitation, and immoral behavior), and administrative/regulatory violations such as failure to report, continuing education lapses, and non-compliance with board orders.

profession_specific.laser_procedures_aut.rationale: The items cluster naturally into specific named surgical procedures (capsulotomy, trabeculoplasty, iridotomy), diagnostic-only laser authorization, broad/general laser authority granted by rule or statute, and a residual bucket for procedures like corneal cross-linking, IPL, and non-laser light therapy that don't fit the named surgical clusters.

profession_specific.minor_surgical_proce.rationale: These nine buckets map cleanly onto the distinct anatomical targets and procedure types that appear repeatedly across states: foreign body removal (cornea/conjunctiva/eyelid), corneal surface procedures (scraping/debridement/puncture), eyelash epilation, lacrimal system work (plugs/dilation/irrigation/probing), eyelid lesion excision/drainage/chalazion management, injections (subconj/intralesional/botulinum/epinephrine), light/device therapies (IPL, LipiFlow, intranasal stimulators), wound repair and suture removal, and broad/general authorizations that do not fit a specific category.
